features.name: Eye of the Sahara
features.description: The Richat Structure is a 50 km-wide circular geological formation in the Sahara Desert. Visible from space, it was once thought to be a meteorite impact crater but is now understood to be an eroded geological dome exposing concentric layers of rock over 100 million years old.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Some theorists believe it is the remains of Atlantis.

features.name: Nazca Lines
features.description: Ancient geoglyphs etched into the Nazca Desert depicting animals, plants, and geometric shapes. Created between 500 BCE and 500 CE by removing red pebbles to reveal white ground beneath. Some figures span over 370 metres and are best seen from the air.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: The largest figure is over 370 metres long.

features.name: Magnetic Hill
features.description: A gravity hill near Leh, India, where the surrounding landscape creates an optical illusion making a slight downhill slope appear to be an uphill ascent. Vehicles left in neutral appear to roll 'uphill' against gravity, attracting tourists from around the world.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: The Indian Air Force has reported that aircraft experience unusual magnetic interference in the area.

features.name: Danakil Depression
features.description: One of the hottest, driest, and lowest places on Earth at 125 metres below sea level. Features toxic yellow sulphur springs, lava lakes, and salt formations that resemble an alien landscape. Temperatures regularly exceed 50°C.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Called 'the cruellest place on Earth' — yet extremophile microbes thrive in its acid pools.

features.name: Chocolate Hills
features.description: Over 1,260 perfectly cone-shaped hills spread across 50 square kilometres in Bohol, Philippines. In the dry season, the grass covering them turns brown, giving them their chocolate appearance. Their exact geological origin remains debated.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Local legend says they were formed from the tears of a giant.

features.name: Salar de Uyuni
features.description: The world's largest salt flat at over 10,000 square kilometres. When covered by a thin layer of water, it becomes the world's largest mirror, perfectly reflecting the sky. Contains 50–70% of the world's known lithium reserves.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: It is so flat that satellites use it to calibrate their altimeters.

features.name: Door to Hell
features.description: The Darvaza gas crater is a 70-metre-wide burning pit in the Karakum Desert that has been continuously burning since 1971. Soviet geologists set it alight expecting it to burn out in weeks — it has burned for over 50 years.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Explorer George Kourounis became the first person to descent to the bottom in 2013.

features.name: Giant's Causeway
features.description: Approximately 40,000 interlocking basalt columns formed by an ancient volcanic fissure eruption 50–60 million years ago. The columns are mostly hexagonal, with some having four, five, seven, or eight sides, and some reaching 12 metres tall.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Legend says the Irish giant Fionn mac Cumhaill built it to fight a Scottish giant.

features.name: Lake Natron
features.description: An extremely alkaline salt lake in Tanzania with a pH up to 12 and temperatures reaching 60°C. Its caustic waters can calcify animals that die in it, preserving them in eerie stone-like forms. The red colour comes from salt-loving microorganisms.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Despite its lethality, it is the sole breeding ground for 2.5 million lesser flamingos.

features.name: Blood Falls
features.description: A crimson-coloured outflow of iron-rich brine seeping from Taylor Glacier in Antarctica. The water comes from a subglacial lake sealed beneath the glacier for over 2 million years. The red colour is caused by iron oxidising on contact with air.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Microbes living in the brine survive without oxygen or sunlight.

features.name: Fairy Circles
features.description: Millions of mysterious circular bare patches dotting the grasslands of Namibia and Western Australia. Each circle is ringed by taller grass. Scientists have debated for decades whether they are caused by termites, self-organising plant competition, or a combination of both.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Local legend says they are footprints of the gods.

features.name: Sailing Stones
features.description: Rocks in Death Valley's Racetrack Playa that move across the flat desert floor, leaving long tracks behind them — without any human or animal intervention. Scientists discovered in 2014 that thin sheets of ice pushed by light winds are responsible.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Some rocks weigh over 300 kg yet still glide across the playa.

features.name: Stonehenge
features.description: A prehistoric stone circle erected in stages from approximately 3000 to 2000 BCE on Salisbury Plain, England. The largest stones weigh 25 tonnes and were transported over 200 km from Wales. Its exact purpose — astronomical observatory, temple, or healing site — remains debated.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Aligned with the sunrise on the summer and winter solstices.

features.name: Easter Island Moai
features.description: Nearly 900 monolithic human figures carved by the Rapa Nui people between 1250 and 1500 CE. The tallest erected moai is 10 metres high and weighs 82 tonnes. They were moved kilometres from the quarry, likely by 'walking' them using ropes.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Most moai face inland to watch over the villages, not out to sea.

features.name: Xuankong Temple
features.description: The Hanging Temple built into a cliff face 75 metres above the ground near Mount Heng, China. Built in 491 CE, it is the only existing temple combining Buddhism, Taoism, and Confucianism. Its 40 halls and pavilions are supported by slender wooden pillars.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: The crossbeams were inserted into holes chiselled into the cliff face like giant chopsticks.

features.name: Great Pyramid of Giza
features.description: The oldest and largest of the three pyramids on the Giza plateau, built around 2560 BCE as a tomb for Pharaoh Khufu. Originally 146 metres tall, it was the tallest man-made structure for over 3,800 years. Consists of roughly 2.3 million limestone blocks.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: The four sides are aligned to the cardinal compass points with extraordinary accuracy.

features.name: Petra
features.description: An ancient city carved directly into rose-red sandstone cliffs by the Nabataeans over 2,000 years ago in what is now Jordan. Half-built and half-carved into rock, it was a major trading hub. Its Treasury façade stands 40 metres tall.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Only 15% of the city has been explored by archaeologists.

features.name: Angkor Wat
features.description: The largest religious monument in the world, built in the early 12th century as a Hindu temple and gradually transformed into a Buddhist site. Covering 162 hectares, it is an architectural masterpiece featuring bas-reliefs stretching over 800 metres.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: More stone was used in Angkor Wat than in all the Egyptian pyramids combined.

features.name: Mariana Trench
features.description: The deepest known oceanic trench on Earth, plunging to 10,935 metres at Challenger Deep. Only four crewed descents have reached the bottom. The pressure at the bottom is over 1,000 atmospheres — enough to crush most submarines.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: If you placed Mount Everest at the bottom, its peak would still be over 2 km underwater.

features.name: Spotted Lake
features.description: A saline endorheic lake near Osoyoos, British Columbia. In summer as water evaporates, it leaves behind large polka-dot mineral pools of magnesium sulphate, calcium, and sodium sulphate. Each pool's colour depends on its mineral concentration.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: The Syilx First Nation considers it a sacred healing site called Kliluk.
